passages.title: A Saving Countermelody
passages.text:
As you row towards the island, the singing becomes louder.
You wave to your crew. Rafael takes out his accordion, Gregory plays his trombone, and Audrie strums her guitar.
Their dissonant music tears the haunting harmony of the song, and the fish-faced man tears the fins from his head.
“Stop this noise!” » he shouts.
Through your notes, you hear the sirens humming strange words about the god Thrack, but their charm can no longer reach you.
“Enjoy your stay here,” you said, leaving the man on the shore before returning to the Manticore.
🎶 The crew plays music to counter the spell of the sirens.
💰 Earn 2 coins
⭐ Earn 1 XP
📜 Complete the quest 30 and win the quest 31.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Howl from the Depths
passages.text:
You grab the fishman and throw him overboard.
Its cry disappears into the waves, but the song immediately transforms into an atrocious howl, twisting your spirits.
The crew is at the end of their nerves...
At least the unfortunate man left his bag behind.
💰 Earn 3 coins ⚓ +1 Low morale 🌀 +1 Madness
⭐ +2 XP
📜 Lose the quest 30.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Island of the Forbidden Song
passages.text:
“Are you sure this is where you live? » you ask the fish-faced traveler.
The sea is rough, the sky heavy with heavy rain clouds.
“Oh yes,” he replies, licking his lips. “We're almost there. » A few minutes later, a strange voice rises from the wind, singing a haunting melody.
“Stop the ship!” We have arrived! » he says, running to the railing and greeting a small rocky island looming in the mist.
“Come and meet my friends,” he adds.
The song from the island bewitches you.
You now understand the words:
“Illustrious Sofi, listen to our two voices.
We know your journey, and can show you the way home. » 🏝️ You reach an island from which a fascinating song emanates, which your guide claims to be his home.
A. Brave the island.
🧠 Cunning 8 ❌ Fail: goes to 171.4 ✅ Pass: goes to 171.1
B. Throw the man into the sea and flee.
💪 Strength 6 ❌ Failure: ❤️ –2 Health, 🌀 +1 Madness.
✅ Success: goes to 171.2

passages.title: The Song of Madness
passages.text:
As you approach the island, the singing becomes deafening.
You wave to your crew. Rafael, Gregory and Audrie begin their musical uproar again.
But this time, the fishman snatches their instruments and throws them into the sea before diving in after them.
The enchantment of the sirens then insinuates itself into your minds, engraving in you the secret songs of the god Thrack.
You return to the Manticore, but the melody screams in your head for days, gradually eating away at your sanity.
⚓ +3 Low morale 🌀 +1 Madness
📜 Lose the quest 30 and win the quest 31.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Brother Found
passages.text:
“Thank you so much! » said the man, panting, still out of breath from his flight.
“I knew they were after me, but I thought I could outrun them…” Audrie crosses her arms.
“Was this all worth risking your neck for?” Your sister was consumed with worry! » The man laughed nervously.
“Ah, but now neither my sister nor I will ever have to worry about that again! I found gold! For real this time! And I am happy to share a little of my fortune with those who saved my life. » 💬 A man chased by wild beasts thanks you for your help.
💰 Earn 8 coins
⭐ Earn 2 XP
📜 Complete the quest 67 and win the quest 63.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Gold Rush
passages.text:
The camp has transformed into a real small mining town.
The plank cabins line up in the snow, and the sound of pickaxes echoes in the hills.
The prospector and his sister come running to meet you.
“Thank you for saving my brother!” » exclaims the young girl.
“Thanks to you, the mine is prospering!” » adds the prospector. “We are always looking for strong arms. We pay well for an honest day's work, if you're interested. » 💬 The prospector you rescued offers you work in his gold mine.
A. Working in the mine.
💪 Strength 8 ❌ Failure: ❤️ –5 Health (a misplaced hammer blow causes a cave-in) ✅ Success: goes to 172.3
B. Politely refuse and leave.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: An Honest Day's Work
passages.text:
After so many adventures in this strange world, manual work in the mine seems almost soothing to you.
The gold dust sticks to your skin, but the reward is honest.
💰 Earn 3 coins.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: Flight Along the Shore
passages.text:
You spot a camp on the shore, exactly where the little girl described it.
And you arrive just in time: a man is running along the beach, chased by several monstrous creatures!
“A yeti!” » shouts Rafael.
“A puma!” » Gregory shouts.
“By gods…a mammoth?!” » Audrie chokes.
💬 A man is hunted by wildlife as ferocious as it is improbable.
⚔️ Combat 59, 60, 61 (Level 21)
→ Go to paragraph 172.1

The air in the passage reeks of decomposition.
Each breath claws at your throat like a rusty blade.
You prefer to retreat, without taking anything.

Moss piles up in the bay, below the cliffs, forming towers of gray foam like tin skyscrapers.
Leaning against the rocks, entwined by heavy chains, lies the naked body of a man.

passages.title: The Freed Prisoner
passages.text:
You cautiously approach the chained man.
His body is relaxed, and his eyes look like two pools of blood and milk.
“Does he see us? It seems that he is no longer in this world..." Audrie pulls on the chains: they fall to the ground with a heavy clank.
A hoarse cry burst from the man's throat.
“Free!” Oh, thank you! » Without warning, he leaps from the top of the cliff and dives into the sea, swimming with ease towards the Manticore.
On board, he asks for food and clothes, then gives you a grateful smile.
“These chains were enchanted. I could never have freed myself from it alone.
You saved me. Now I must return to my treasure — if it is still there.
Take me, and I will reward you. »
💰 Earn 2 coins.
📜 Receive the 12 (Ubzon) adventure map.
📜 Win the quests 14 and 15.
→ Return to the ship.

On a wall hangs a corpse dressed in a striped suit, a smile frozen on its whitened head.
On the stone table in front of him, a sign inscribed by hand:
“Take just one. » In front of the carefully dressed skeleton, a small pile of treasures waits, gleaming in the torchlight.
A. Respect the last wishes of the deceased.
→ Go to 169
B. Take more than your share.
→ Go to 169.1

You dismount and explore the inside of the gigantic skull of a titanic creature, a vestige of a monster from another age.
While you are searching a pile of stones, scorpions appear and sting your crew.

passages.title: Valard's Footprints
passages.text:
You search the sand, looking for the four-toed tracks of the legendary Valard.
Inside the colossal sun-bleached skull, you discover the footprint — deeply marked in the dried mud: four notches in each step.
You follow the trail through the skull, along what's left of the spine, then out into the open desert.
For hours, you walk in the sand bristling with stones, until you finally reach an ancient pedestal.
In its center is a huge stone hammer, anchored as if it refuses to be touched.
A. Extract the hammer by force.
🪓 STRENGTH 8 ❌ Failure: ❤️ –3 Health, 💢 +2 Weakened.
→ Go to 176.2
B. Give up and start again.
💰 +1 piece.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.text:
With a roar, you snatch the hammer from the pedestal, brandishing it towards the burning sky.
The sun reflects off the rough stone, and a wave of power passes through your arm.

passages.title: The Quays of Alzarria
passages.text:
If the keyword WELL is entered, 👉 go to 177.5.
You dock at the docks of the southern gate of Alzarria, then venture into the immense city.
A guard in scale armor gives you a curt nod as you wander through the bazaar.
Colorful awnings hang between the tall clay houses, casting their shadow on the cyclopean street teeming with merchants, travelers, mercenaries, jugglers, children, mules and chickens.
As you examine a stall overflowing with red, oblong fruits, a grimy-faced beggar hisses something at you.
Kasumi approaches to understand.
But the man moves with the speed of a snake: he hits Kasumi in the jaw with a sharp blow. Three other beggars emerge from the shadows, grab it, and all disappear into an alley.
You rush after them — but the alley is empty. They vanished.
A. Search the alleys for Kasumi.
🚫 You cannot use Kasumi for this test.
👁️ PERCEPTION 8 ❌ Failure: ❤️ –8 Health (thieves attack you in an alley).
→ Go to 177.1

🧠 CONNAISSANCE 9 ❌ Failure: ❤️ –3 Health, 😞 +2 Morale Low (you knock over a meat stall and suffer the wrath of several merchants).
→ Go to 177.2

The streets of Alzarria form a veritable labyrinth of ancient stones, abandoned houses and hidden gardens.

passages.title: The Fruit Seller
passages.text:
You question a plump saleswoman at the stall overflowing with fruit.
His smile is fine, almost complicit.
“I saw your friend leave…” she whispers hoarsely.
“Many of those who look like beggars here belong to a secret order.
They are fascinated by strangers — and often abduct them.
» “Where can we find them?” » you ask.
“In the canals, under the city. Beware of rats. » She shows you the way and offers you a sample from her stall.
🥕 +1 Vegetables.

passages.title: The Red Jackal's Cistern
passages.text:
The murmur of water hides your steps as you descend into a vast cistern.
In the center, a plunge pool reflects daylight filtering through openings in the ceiling, from which countless buckets hang like ripe fruit.
On the opposite bank, a group of beggars are busy.
You see Kasumi, covered in dust, tied to a wooden post.
Above them floats a frayed banner representing a red jackal.
“Tell us about cars!” » cries a beggar.
" Yes ! What are they for? Can we use them for cooking? » adds another.
You burst out of the shadows, slamming into the group like a rugby player, and cut Kasumi's bonds.
The dazed beggars slowly get up and line up, ready to fight under their frayed banners.
⚔️ COMBAT 10, 11, 25 (Level 14)
→ Go to 177.4

The clan of beggars disperses in the labyrinth of canals, and you return to the streets of Alzarria alongside Kasumi.
“Stop me from talking to beggars next time,” she growls.
“At least, not in this town,” you reply.

passages.text:
A small port town rests between two mountains, at the end of a long bay.
His buildings are an incoherent assemblage of wood, brick and stone — architectural chaos with no apparent logic.
The inhabitants of Porthaven are like the city: an improbable mix.
Ordinary humans from all corners of the Wandering Sea rub shoulders seamlessly with monstrous creatures, all busy with their daily routines.
Not far from you, a sea serpent bargains fiercely with a mythan seller for some fruit, while a floating eye brushes past you without paying attention.

→ Go to 179.1

Requires the keyword HONOR.
→ Go to 179.5
D. Follow Kannan, who has moved away.
Requires the keyword GHOST.
→ Go to 179.6
E. Leave town.
→ Return to the ship.

“Your work is of rare delicacy,” she said to the merchant—a humanoid rat with gray fur and gentle eyes.
Despite the fantastic nature of the items, their prices are surprisingly low.

passages.title: Wayfinder's Offer
passages.text:
The Wayfinder office overlooks the bay from a white stone building.
Through the large window, the quays are visible in their entirety.
“If we are attacked, I want to be the first to know,” he said calmly.
“Those who live here fear the awakening of the gods—that they will reclaim their power and rob us of free will.
You fear that they will sleep forever, condemning you to wander far from your homes. » He pauses for a moment, then continues in a more serious tone:
“But there is a solution to both problems.
The gods claim to be absolute and infinite, but there were others before them, forgotten, long dead, and yet possessing the same power.
Power is eternal — but not those who wield it.
If we can take this power away without killing them, they will become mortal again. And this power... I will be able to channel it to open a portal to your world. » Gregory leans forward:
"Why don't you send your own people to find these forgotten totems?" » “Because they don’t want any more war,” Wayfinder replies.
“And I fear that violence will be necessary to obtain them. I can't force this on them... but I can ask you.
If you help me, we can all get what we want. »

“You are not of this world. You are looking for Totems to awaken the gods. They promised you a return home.

passages.title: The Cult of the Herring King

The man who answers you wears a fabric headdress representing a red herring swallowing his head.
“What are we doing?” Can't you see it? We are preparing the ceremony! » Gregory gives a smile.
“Sorry for asking…but you worship a fish god?” » “Not a god,” the man corrects. “A king. King Herring, to be precise.

“If you want to do us a favor, you could go get something for the ceremony.
It’s essential, but we can’t travel.
We will pay. » “And what should we bring back?” » “The blood of the oldest fisherman in the world,” he answers naturally.

→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Ghost in the Mechanism
passages.text:
Audrie methodically dismantles the metal body.
When the last piece comes loose, a violent wind sweeps the island.
When it calms down, a spectral figure floats in front of you.
“An artisan once tried to lock a fragment of our essence into this form.
We were divided over the quest for the body, and we remain divided over your decision to free us from it.
Neither gratitude nor anger. » The wind rises again, and the entity vanishes, carried away like mist.
💰 +5 parts 🪵 +3 Materials
📜 Win the quest 164.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: Puffin Rock
passages.text:
A few puffins nest on a deserted islet, placed on the waves like a black and white jewel.
A. Attempt to fish nearby.
🎓 SAVVY 6 ❌ Failure: 😞 Laurent wins 1 Low Morale.
→ Go to 199.4

→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: Laurent's Catch
passages.text:
While fishing, Laurent never stops chattering about the “real” techniques of seasoned sailors.
The afternoon loses serenity, but his advice bears fruit: the catch is abundant.
🍖 +2 Meat.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Deceitful Merchant's Prison
passages.text:
Ubzon chuckles softly at your defeat.
You are sent to a dungeon beneath the pyramid, where you spend several days brooding over your failure and looking for a way out.
But the more hunger weakens you, the more your hope of escape dwindles.
A few days later, the guards throw a new prisoner into your cell — a woman from Zokmere, recognizable by her green shirt made of sewn pieces.
“So, Ubzon tricked you too,” she said.
“I met him at Zokmere market. He promised me mountains and wonders...
And here I am. Did you find a way to escape?
I can force a lock, if we work together.
Otherwise, one of the guards seemed more...friendly. We could try to talk to him. » You are locked in the Ubzon dungeon, with a fellow inmate ready to collaborate to escape.

passages.title: The Wager of Lies
passages.text:
Ubzon enters the game with undisguised pleasure, quickly mastering the Cunnings of the game.
One by one, your companions are eliminated, until only the two of you remain.
Your hand shows three of a kind, while doubt passes through Ubzon's milky eyes.
“All in,” you said, pushing your winnings towards the center of the table.
Ubzon laughs, convinced you're bluffing.
When the cards fall, he only has two pairs.
“Well done,” he said coldly. “Go, you’re free. » The return to the ship is perilous, but among your gains is a totem engraved with strange symbols.

⭐ +1 XP

passages.title: The Queen's Move
passages.text:
Ubzon sits at the table, eager for strategy.
In a few rounds, he understands the game.
You exchange piece by piece, until there are only six pawns each remaining.
You advance your queen in a risky maneuver; Ubzon takes the bait.
“Checkmate,” you said calmly.
Ubzon smiled, amused by his own defeat.
On the way back, Audrie hands you a carved stone.
“I stole it from the pyramid while Ubzon was playing,” she said with a wink.
💰 +4 parts
⭐ +1 XP
📜 Receive the adventure card 43 (Totem: Stone of Deception)
📜 Complete the quest 15.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: Escape and Liberation
passages.text:
Ubzon flees and you free his prisoners.
In the corridors of the pyramid, you discover strange symbols and relics engraved with the image of the god Zacra.
You bring back with you a sacred totem with a glowing heart.
💰 +8 parts
⭐ +4 XP
📜 Receive the adventure card 43 (Totem: Stone of Deception)
📜 Complete the quest 15.
→ Return to the ship.

“Mara Johnson, by all means…come in!” » Mac insists that you stop by to say hello to an old friend.

passages.title: Old Stories
passages.text:
“This is Carolina, we traveled together for a while,” Mac explains as he enters.
The interior of the cottage is simple and almost empty, the walls bare, the furniture sparse.
“I’m moving soon, so I put everything away. But come, sit down,” said Carolina.
In the kitchen, around a large wooden table, the two women remember their adventures.
“And you, how many years has it been since you left piracy? » says Mac, laughing.
“I like to point out that, but I was only a pirate for a few months! » replies Carolina.
“The job of lumberjack suits me much better. » The tone relaxes, the conversation becomes lively, and soon the whole crew is laughing around the meal.
Before your departure, Carolina offers you some provisions:
“Take these provisions, it will make it easier for me to carry around. And then, this is my way of saying thank you. » 🍞 +2 Grains 🥕 +2 Vegetables 🪵 +1 Material 💬 Remove any Low Morale.
📜 Win the quest 51.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: Caught in the Act
passages.text:
You are tinkering with the vegetable garden to make it look like an animal attack when Mac and Carolina come out of the cottage and surprise you.
Carolina stares at you, disappointed.
“I know it's a tough world, but I'm really disappointed, Mac. » “I didn’t know about it, Carolina… and I’ll tell you, I’m disappointed too,” Mac replies.
“Take what you want, I’m moving soon.” But…
don't kill my chickens. » Mac looks away, visibly hurt by your behavior.

→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Empty Cottage
passages.text:
The cottage is abandoned, the garden withered.
On the door, an illegible note, eaten away by the rain, indicates that one day someone wanted to leave an address.
There's nothing left.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Fish Offering
passages.text:
The fish glides through the sea, beating the water with its tail in a happy swirl.
Moments later, he returns to the ship, spewing a shower of glittering silver coins onto the deck.

passages.text:
Despite the crew's best efforts, no blade or harpoon can pierce the fish's shiny scales.
After a futile struggle, the creature wriggles out of reach and disappears into the waves, leaving behind a feeling of failure.
😞 Win 1 Low Morale.
⚓ Lose 1 Command.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Stone of Chains
passages.text:
You help unload the crates from the small crashed plane, while throwing a few light barbs to ease tensions.
Rafael, who was trying to turn the crew against you, ends up giving up, with a closed face, and returns to the Manticore without a word.
While searching the deceased pilot's jacket, you discover a stone engraved with strange symbols, still warm despite the cold of the surrounding metal.

“Rafael, one day in prison for sowing discord. » “Captain, I didn’t mean it like that…” he tries, through gritted teeth.
You wave to Kannan and Laurent, who escort him to the ship without another word.
Before leaving, the crew methodically searched the wreckage, recovering some food and the pilot's personal effects.
In his jacket, you again find an engraved stone, similar to those of the forgotten gods.
💰 +3 Coins 🪨 Get the adventure card 55 — Totem: Stone of Chains

“Beneath the streets of Alzarria, in the canals and cisterns, lies a rare relic: the Incense of Meecra.
I've been looking for her for years... without success. As much as someone else benefits from it. » He is silent for a moment, then gives a hint of a smile.
“Would you like any further advice?” »
A. Offer some food to listen to what he has to say.

→ Return to the ship.

“I'm looking for the god Thrack. You and these snakes will help me.
Either you accept, or... I release them on your ship. »

A one-eyed Pann, introducing himself as Captain Tarr, answers you with a mocking smile.

“Yes… that’s her. The Stone of Wind and Waves.

The airy caves offer a welcome respite from the furnace of the desert.
At the center of a natural amphitheater stands a stone palace, sculpted with divine precision.
White statues line a corridor, serene faces, hair blowing in the wind.
On a pedestal, an engraved inscription attracts your attention.

passages.title: Venme's Grandfather
passages.text:
A layer of gray dust covers what was once a welcoming home: a colorful rug, three carved chairs, two beds still carefully made.
In the small kitchen, an old man sits, focused on repairing a worn fishing rod.
Venme suddenly steps forward and slaps his face.
“You left us alone, and everything fell apart,” she spits.
The old man raises his head, his eyes moist.
“Oh… Venme, you found me. I am so ashamed to have left. But your grandmother... she didn't want me anymore. » Sales remain prohibited.
“She told me she begged you to stay. » The old man chuckles weakly, before a coughing fit interrupts him.
" What ? No... she told me to leave. So I came back here.
I was hoping to start hunting for totems again, but I only found one. » He takes down the engraved stone he wore around his neck and hands it to his granddaughter.
“Keep it.” And stay a little, will you? Does your grandmother know you're here? » “Grandma is dead,” Venme replies in a broken voice.
A heavy silence settles in.
The old man nods slowly, unable to speak further.
On the way back, Venme walks alongside you.
“I think I'll stay here, with my grandfather,” she said softly.
“But I wish you luck on your journey.” » She gives you her grandfather's totem, symbol of a late reconciliation.

Venme comes out, furious, and punches him in the face.
“You left us alone, and everything fell apart! » “Come… you found me. I was wrong, I know. But your grandmother didn't want me anymore. » “She begged you to stay!” » Venme replies, his voice trembling.
“No… she chased me away,” the old man coughs. “I was about to go back and look for the totems, but I only found this one. Take it. And stay with me, will you? » “Grandma is dead,” Venme whispers.
The old man is silent and slowly hands him his carved totem.
On the way back, Venme accompanies you to the Manticore.
“I'll stay here, Captain. Thanks for everything. »

The heat made her suffer. Here, in the cold, we are finally at peace. » Audrie steps forward, hesitant:

" No. We want to experience material life for a time. But in return for your help, we offer you knowledge:
look for one of our totems in the Mirror Forest to the south.
Be Cunnings, and don't get lost. » ✨ The robot reveals its spiritual origin and tells you the location of a totem.

a pair of strange glasses, with lenses cut from a translucent ruby, which shine with an almost living glow in the dim light.

»

passages.title: Flight and Fall
passages.text:

The Manticore sinks under a swarm of skeletons.
You find refuge on a merchant ship, but the price is heavy: the dispersion of your crew.
You end up settling in Zokmere, living in quiet success... haunted by the memory of your loved ones.

“My friends! What a joy to see you again! » The shadow creature sees you, a distorted smile on its lips, while the chained villagers stop in their tracks, their eyes full of anger.
“Look how beautiful this city is, thanks to your precious advice. Stay for dinner so I can tell you the details..."

passages.title: The Sleeping God's Judgment
passages.text:
The ground trembles beneath your feet.
A colossal voice, like suppressed thunder, resonates in the depths of the earth.
“I know your minds.
Your quest will fail.
I will make sure of it. » The walls split, the stones detached from the ceiling with a deafening roar.
The divine breath causes a landslide, forcing you to retreat towards the ship.

passages.title: Raltolde's Blessing
passages.text:
This time, the same voice resonates, but without anger.
A kind warmth runs through your body, as if the sea itself enveloped you in gratitude.
“I know your minds.
Your quest is blessed by those who long for peace. » A gentle wind sweeps away the dust — the stones freeze, the shadows recede.
⭐ +3 XP
📜 Complete the quest 127.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: Raltolde's Command
passages.text:
The god whispers, and his words are engraved in your flesh.
“I know your minds.
You are indecisive and weak.
Choose — and be brave in your choice, for without courage you will fail. » The echo fades away, but its warning continues to resonate in your mind.
😔 +1 Low morale
📜 Lose the quest 127.
→ Return to the ship.

passages.title: The Hectakron's Return
passages.text:
The monster emerges from the abyss with a titanic crash.
The Hectakron hits the hull, twisting the steel like wood.
Its immense jaws tear off the bow of the ship — your world turns upside down.
Someone is screaming. You grab onto a ladder, breathless.
The icy water crushes you against the wall, filling your lungs, stifling your last prayer.
“Father… I will never see New York again. » 🌊 THE END (END 7)

passages.text:
The mythans set fire to the bridge.
The flames devour the ropes, the sails, the screams.
You plunge into the liquid night, watching your Manticore slowly sink, like a wounded beast sinking into the grave.
You look for your companions… in vain.
Your arms are weakening. The abyss embraces you.
You think of your father one last time.
“He will never know how far I have come. » 🌊 THE END (END 8)

passages.text:
A tectonic rumble vibrates every beam of the Manticore.
The walls are screaming. The monster bursts from the abyss, tearing the sea apart.
Its jaws drop—the metal gives way, the lights go out.
The cold, the pressure, the fear.
And suddenly everything goes silent.
“Father… I failed. » 🌊 THE END (END 9)

passages.title: Ohmlude's Call
passages.text:
A figure forms in the dust—a small, round woman, a nest of gray hair, slightly translucent. Her smile is apple-shaped, and in her right hand she holds a long bamboo fishing rod. This is the same woman you first met on the rocky outcrop: Ohmlude, the goddess.
“Time is up. The Hectakron wants to reign over these seas, without rival among the gods. He found you and grew strong enough to destroy you. It's now or never: you'll need all the help you can get. Even if you push it away today, it will come back tomorrow, then the day after that, and it won't stop until it sinks your ship. » She disappears.
🔧 Immediate effects:
• Restore full health to crew members.
• Remove all status tokens (including Low Morale) and any Fatigue.
• Return all Order tokens, Adventure cards and crew boards.
• Earn 7 Orders (+1 per player) and distribute them as desired between players.
⭐ You can now spend your unused XP Points to purchase level cards.

passages.title: The Island of the Gods
passages.text:
As the creature darkens, the sky becomes strange:
alien star patterns, shifting horizon. Before you, a solitary island of stone rises. White columns form a circle around a central tower — a place both sinister and familiar: where the gods sleep.
If you don't have any totems, go to F20. Otherwise, continue.
You approach and climb a cracked staircase leading to the tower. The air is still, almost stale; white sand sticks to the steps and glows in the dark night. The tower is hollow, an endless flight of steps runs along the wall.
On the way up, rear footsteps echo: a motley group blocks the entrance — Lukran soldiers, Zokmere hunters, Pann archers. A man takes off his crimson helmet; his wrinkled eyes beg you:
“Don’t wake the gods. They will strike these seas. » Mac squeezes your arm, cold: “Ignore them. We're almost there. » The armored man puts down his helmet gently. “Give us the totems. We followed you — you lasted longer than the others, faced the Hectakron. But it doesn’t have to end like this. » A Pann woman steps forward, her bioluminescent skin turning pale. “Our people suffered to defy the gods. Give up.
Stay with us. » Choice:
A. Run to the top of the tower — → F7.
B. Say that you plan to destroy the gods. (requires keyword FROG) — → F8.

passages.title: The Top of the Tower
passages.text:
You draw destiny.
➡️ If you have the keyword SPARRING, add +2 to your draw.
• If the result is 14, continue below.
• If the result is 5 or higher, go to F6.
You reach the top of the tower. In a vast circular room, the gods rest on stone slabs cut into a circle.
They seem more dead than asleep — motionless, breathless, drained of all heat.
The first is a plump woman with gray hair:
Ohmlude.
Beside him, a woman with brown skin and dark hair, holding a shell and a flute.
“It’s Meecra,” Mac whispers, pointing at her.
Mac continues:
— Zacra, god of tricks and captives, handsome man with a necklace of coins, gray temples.
— Shorme, pale goddess of earthquakes, her closed eyes still quivering with anger.
— Valard, in red armor, clutching a spear and a curved saber.
— Orfash, god of the mythans, with the head of a bull, gigantic.
— Finally, an old bearded man, dressed in a simple robe, whose slab is covered with grass and vines.
An eighth tile is empty — marked only with a crumpled feather.
"We need to place a totem on each tile to wake them up," Mac said in a low voice.

passages.title: The Awakening of the Gods
passages.text:
The totems light up with a blinding glow. The light runs along the slabs and reaches the inert bodies of the gods.
A breath sweeps through the room—heavy, ancient, saturated with power. The gods' eyelids lift.
They stand up, alive again.
The next moment, they are aboard the Manticore.
Some laugh, speaking of the vengeance to come against the peoples of the Wandering Sea.
Others whisper that their awakening was inevitable, that the power of the totems would have called them back sooner or later.
None thank the crew. None of them really look at you.
One after the other, they fly above the waves, leaving behind them flashes of gold and wind.
Only Ohmlude, the fishing goddess, remains.
Mac calls out to him:
“You’re not going to send us home?” » Ohmlude stops, sighs, then smiles:
“So be it. I don't want you here anyway... You'd make too much of a fuss. » She jumped out of the ship.
A stone column springs from the ocean to receive it.
Ohmlude inhales deeply — and spits up a storm.
The winds are unleashed, the sea rears up, the sky roars. Then everything calms down.
In the distance, the mist rises over the familiar silhouette of New York.
“It’s strange… I feel like it’s the dream now. » You and Gregory silently watch your companions get off the ship, their arms full of their belongings, their eyes moist.
“Second chances change people,” Gregory said.
“We see life differently when we almost lose it. » You take a deep breath, facing the hazy sun.
“I think I see it clearly now. » A slow smile stretches across your face.
“We would never have survived without you, Captain,” Gregory adds.
You place a hand on his shoulder.
He nods and leaves the ship.
Later, in the quiet room where your father is waiting for you, you realize how distant it all seems.
His hand trembles slightly as he squeezes it in yours.
“You make me proud, Sofi. You are so strong... I should have been a better father, but you never needed me. » You stroke his forehead gently.
“I’m happy to have you, Dad. » He smiled weakly.
“Thank you for asking me to come. I wasn’t sure you would… It was so far away. » A discreet laugh.
“Not too far,” you say, smiling.
He closes his eyes.
“My daughter, the captain of the ship…” And his face calms down.
⚓ END — Ending 3: The Return to New York Note the totems found on the achievement sheet.

passages.title: The End of the Gods
passages.text:
You move confidently forward, the mechanical toad in your arms—this cold, strange artifact, forged to do the unthinkable.
The gods lie peacefully around you.
The time has come.
You place the machine on the ground and open its steel mouth.
One after the other, you place all the totem stones collected during your journey.
The toad's eyes light up with an unearthly glow.
A rumble rises. Then, a blast of lightning shot out, striking the divine tiles.
Lightning ricochets from one body to another, lacerating immortal flesh, splitting stone, tearing the sky.
The gods writhe in the light, then collapse silently.
Soon all that remains of them is a cloud of golden dust.
A translucent silhouette crosses the tower wall.
It's Vyme.
She gazes at the empty tiles, translucent tears shining on her pale cheeks.
“They’re gone…” she whispers.
“I can’t believe it… It worked. » A few weeks later, the news spread:
The gods are dead.
The king and queen of Zokmere invite you to live in their city.
A fleet escorts you to their tropical island.
When you arrive, the port is ablaze with music and light
— seven days of celebration, dances and songs to your glory.
The months pass. The Manticore remains in port, its sails folded.
The crew members leave one after the other, each finding their own way.
Gregory, now settled in Zokmere, sits one morning on the quay, a cup of steaming tea in his hands.
In the distance, fishing boats leave the turquoise bay.
“It’s strange,” he said. “I find it hard to believe that anyone ever thought of waking up these gods. » You join him on the edge of the pontoon, dangling your legs above the clear water.
“Sometimes you don’t know what you really want…until you choose,” you reply.
A gentle silence settles.
“A part of me shudders to think what this world would have been like if we had done things differently. » You inhale deeply, eyes looking up at the sun.
“I would have liked to see my father again… but I think I finally stopped crying for him. » Gregory nods slowly.
“We would never have survived without you, Captain.
THANKS. » You place a hand on his shoulder.
He stands up, his peaceful gaze turned towards the small clinic he opened on the hill.
⚓ END — Ending 6: Death of the Gods Note the totems found on the achievement sheet.
These totems unlock new cards for your next campaigns.
Indicate the ending obtained and your final score (see rulebook).

passages.title: The Mortal Gods
passages.text:
You finally reach the top of the tower.
The gods rest on a circle of stone slabs, their bodies stretched out in perfect stillness.
Their silence has nothing of sleep: it is cold, absolute, funereal.
The first deity is a plump woman with gray hair
— Ohmlude, the fishing goddess.
Beside him lies Meecra, dark-skinned and fingers resting on a flute and a shell.
Mac points at them, his voice almost trembling.
“And there…Zacra, the god of prisoners and towers.
This one, the pale one with black hair, is Shorme, the goddess of earthquakes.
The one armored in red is Valard, the warrior with the curved saber.
The bull-headed colossus, Orfash, lord of the mythans.
And he, the bearded old man, Loras, master of life and the vines. » An eighth slab is empty — only a dirty feather remains, placed in the center.
“We need to place a totem on each tile to wake them up,” Mac said, in a low voice.
But before you can move, a metallic clank makes your blood run cold.
Rafael has you at gunpoint.
“Give me the totems. » His gaze is hard, without a trace of hesitation.
“I don’t want to go back. I'm done with this sailor's life, toiling for crumbs. These stones... I'm going to sell them here. And finally live. » The crew freezes.
The silence of the sanctuary seems to grow even heavier, as if the gods themselves were holding their breath.
Choice:
A. Try to reason with Rafael.
→ Go to paragraph F13.
B. Discreetly give the signal to stop.
→ Go to paragraph F14.

passages.title: The Race to the Summit
passages.text:
You jump up the steps, panting, as a roar rises behind you.
The crowd began to run, a sea of ​​enraged warriors and archers, their footsteps echoing in the stone.
An arrow whistles through the air. Laurent collapses, his hand on his shoulder.
“Laurent!” » Audrie yells, stopping in her tracks.
But already, he stands up, his features distorted by pain.
Without a word, he turns and rushes straight towards the horde, sword raised, to hold them back.
A second arrow hits him in the chest — and yet he continues to advance, shouting the captain's name before disappearing into the fray.
You remain frozen, paralyzed by stupor, blocking the climb.
Behind you, panic spreads through the group.
Gloria grabs your arm in a firm grip.
“Captain!” Up ! » You regain your senses and stumble up the last steps.
The group rushes into a large circular room, pierced with windows opening onto the black sea.
Rafael and Marco throw themselves against a gigantic statue in the shape of an eye.
With a deafening crash, they knocked her down the stairs, blocking her way up.
Screams and blows echo below, but you know there is no turning back.
The path to the gods is now clear.

passages.title: The Lie or the Revelation
passages.text:
“We originally wanted to wake them up…” you say, your voice firm.
“…but now we intend to destroy them. » Shocked murmurs spread through the crowd.
A man shouts:
“Lie!” » Before anyone reacts, an ethereal form slides out of the wall.
It’s Vyme, translucent and radiant.
“It’s not a lie, my friends,” she said in a resonant voice.
“I have guided these travelers from the beginning to complete the work I began long ago.
They now have what it takes.
And if all goes well... we will finally be freed from the yoke of the gods. » A silence falls.
The soldier in crimson armor slowly lowers his weapon.
He nods, hesitant, but sincere.
“So be it… Pass on.” We let you go. »

“…but now we intend to destroy them. » Voices are immediately raised in the crowd:
“That’s not true!” », “Traitors! » Before the situation escalates, Mac steps forward.
For more than an hour, she speaks, argues, soothes, delivering a speech of rare eloquence.
Little by little, the hostile faces relax.
The weapons are lowered.
The man in scarlet armor sighs, then nods.
" Alright. Whether your intentions are true or not, we will let you pass. »

passages.text:
You triumph in a fierce fight.
The survivors, exhausted and injured, slowly retreated, abandoning the climb.

passages.title: The Choice to Renounce
passages.text:
Deep down, you knew everything would lead to this moment.
You can't condemn an entire world...
Not even to go home.
The totems weigh heavy in your arms — like the burden of your own selfishness.
When you hand them to Pann's wife, a strange lightness comes over you.
She bows her head gravely, and the warriors behind her bow in turn, silent, respectful.
“You will always be welcome in the Wandering Sea,” she said softly.
But this calm does not last.
Until then silent, Mac suddenly bursts out:
“You can’t do that!”
Not after everything we've been through!
I'm going back. I'm going to find my sister, whether you like it or not! » Before anyone could react, she pounced on Pann's wife, snatched several totems from her and fled into the shadows of the temple.
Chaos ensues.
Screams, torches, hurried footsteps.
The crowd scatters in pursuit, but Mac will never be found.
You return to the Manticore, with a heavy heart.
But the respite is short-lived:
the Hectakron, awakened and enraged, finds you.
Its claws lacerate the hull, its jaws shatter the metal.
He will never let you go again.
In a desperate gesture, you order to turn towards the coast.
The Manticore runs aground with a roar of wood and steel — but the crew survives.
The months pass.
You reach Zokmere, the city of refuge where all those who no longer have a home base end up.
Little by little, your companions move away, each following their own path.
One morning, on the quayside bathed in light, Gregory sips his tea while watching the fishing boats leave the bay.
“It’s strange,” he said. “Maybe… this is where I always wanted to live. » You sit next to him, feet dangling above the turquoise water.
“Sometimes you don’t know what you want until you can’t choose anymore,” you whisper.
“And then… I believe that I can live a life here just as full as the one I would have had there. » You inhale deeply, face turned towards the hazy sun.
“And I think I finally stopped crying for my father. » Gregory agrees.
“Yes… but the Manticore? » A slow smile crosses your face.
“I will never be able to get rid of that. » He laughed softly.
“We wouldn’t have survived without you, Captain. THANKS. » You place a hand on his shoulder.
He gets up, stretches, and walks towards his new clinic, at the end of the platform.

“Tie him up,” Mac commands, emotionless.
The crew complies.
Rafael, unconscious, is securely tied to one of the pillars of the sanctuary.
His face, pale and covered in blood, seems frozen between anger and resignation.
Nobody speaks.
The tension hangs in the air — heavy, electric.
But there is no going back.

passages.title: The Mortal Gods: The People's Support
passages.text:
Wayfinder advances in front of the crowd gathered at the foot of the tower.
Faces are closed, weapons tremble in tired hands.
With a soft but confident voice, he speaks.
“We do not seek to dominate the gods, nor to destroy them.
We only want to make them mortal, so that they may share in the fate of the world they have made—and so that they may finally learn what it means to live, to suffer, and to love. » A silence at first. Then, little by little, the murmurs rise.
The doubts fade away, replaced by a strange fervor.
The hunters of Zokmere, the soldiers of Lukra, the warriors of Pann—all begin to applaud, chanting your names.
They stand by your side as you continue your climb.
The gods await you, up there, in their millennial sleep.

passages.title: The Mortal Gods: The Gift of Power
passages.text:
Following Wayfinder's instructions, you place the three Forgotten Gods totems in the center of the sanctuary:
• The Duelist’s Sword, symbol of courage,
• The Mechanical Owl, guardian of knowledge,
• The Stone of Wind and Waves, essence of change.
Wayfinder closes his eyes.
“The power will flow through your being, Captain.
Let it flow towards your purest memory: your home.
What you see in your mind will decide your destination. » He begins an ancient incantation, his voice echoing against the ancient stones.
A purple halo gradually rises from the sleeping bodies of the gods, like a luminous mist pulled out of time.
The energy flows flow slowly towards the totems, then - with a flash - burst into you.
The pain is unbearable.
You feel the power of an entire world beating through your veins.
Your skin burns, your bones vibrate.
Around you, the gods are awakening.
Their looks are empty, helpless.
Zacra, the god of chains, raises his trembling hands:
“What have you done?!” » Wayfinder responds, implacably:
“We have made you mortal.
Live now among us, weak and free. » Valard roars in anger, tries to hit Wayfinder, but he brushes him aside.
“You no longer have any power,” he thunders.
“You will have to learn to live like us. » The power within you intensifies.
Your body threatens to break under the energy it still holds.
Choice:
A. Channel that power into a portal to your home.
→ Go to paragraph F17.
B. Keeping the power for you and your crew.
→ Go to paragraph F18.

passages.title: The Return to New York
passages.text:
You feel immense relief as the power leaves your body.
A flood of purple light invades your field of vision, engulfing you completely.
For a brief moment, you are nothing — neither flesh nor spirit — just a spark carried away in the current of the cosmos.
Then the light fades.
You are on the deck of the Manticore.
The morning mist caresses the ropes, and on the horizon, the silhouette of New York stands up, unreal, bathed in gold and smoke.
Gregory stands by your side.
The other crew members move around, laughing, crying, shouting the names of their loved ones.
They leave the ship one by one, finding a world they thought was lost forever.
Gregory observes the scene in silence.
“It’s strange,” he said softly. “It seems like this is the dream.
Second chances change people.
When death approaches you, you finally learn to look at life differently. » You inhale deeply, raising your face to the pale sun.
“Yes… I think I see it clearly now. » A smile appears on your lips.
Gregory tilts his head.
“We would never have survived without you, Captain.
THANKS. » You place a hand on his shoulder.
He smiles, then walks down the catwalk, joining the resurgent crowd.
Later, you find your father.
His nurse warns you that he has little time left.
So you just stay close to him.
You talk to him about happy memories, about the laughter of yesteryear, and about the sea — always the sea.
He squeezes your hand.
“You make me proud, Sofi. You are so strong. I should have been a better father, but you never needed me. » You stroke his forehead.
“I’m glad to have you, Dad. » “Thank you for asking me to come. » His voice trembles.
“I wasn’t sure you would.” It was so far…” A smile lights up your face.
“Not that far.” » His eyes close in newfound peace.
“My daughter, the captain of the ship…” he whispers.
Sometimes when the breeze picks up over the Hudson, you think of the Wandering Sea.
To the lost islands, to the fallen gods, and to the free souls who still live there.
And you hope that they prosper, now freed from all divine tyranny.

passages.title: The New Gods of the Wandering Sea
passages.text:
You feel the flow of energy swirling through your veins, burning, impossible to contain.
So, slowly, you release some of it back to your crew.
A pulse of pure energy courses through the room — and the world holds its breath.
Before your eyes, your companions change.
Marco's body blurs, splits, multiplies, until a dozen moving shadows stand in his place.
On Kasumi's forehead, two immense bull horns pierce the flesh.
His breathing becomes raspy, almost animalistic.
Living vines wrap around Gregory's arms, growing, flowering, merging with his skin.
As for Audrie, fine rivers of liquid lava flow from her eyes, tracing luminous furrows on her cheeks.
And you — you feel the absolute power taking root in your heart.
Your thoughts expand to encompass the sea, the winds, the entire sky.
Wayfinder staggers.
His gaze, usually calm and wise, is overcome by panic.
“No… no!” » he shouts.
“That wasn’t the plan!” How could you… choose that?
I should never have let you choose! » But it is too late.
The choice is made.
You look at him with cold compassion.
Because now you understand.
You feel the sea breathing through you.
The winds whisper your thoughts.
The islands bend to your will.
You are the new gods of the Wandering Sea.
And your eyes open to an endless world.

passages.title: The Ashes of the Gods
passages.text:
You place, one by one, the totems you own on the stone slabs.
They begin to glow, at first faintly, then more and more brightly, like burning coals fanned by the wind.
A lively warmth fills the room — hope is born in hearts.
Maybe... maybe this is finally the way back?
Maybe you will see New York again, your father, the life before?
The light becomes blinding.
The totems vibrate, whistle, spit sparks…
then, suddenly, disintegrate, reduced to black dust.
Absolute silence falls over the tower.
The slabs, burned, leave only traces of soot.
The gods remain motionless — statues of petrified flesh, frozen in eternal sleep.
Audrie shakes her head, her voice shaking.
“Is that… all?” » Mac remains silent, her gaze fixed on the dark marks.
“I suspected that. We didn't have enough.
But I hoped nonetheless. » You swallow your own dismay, then gather the courage to speak.
“It’s time to accept the truth.
This world is not ours... but nothing stops us from living in it.
Perhaps it is better to leave these people the peace they deserve. » You return to the Manticore.
But barely had the hull returned to the sea when the Hectakron reappeared, attacking the ship, clawing, hitting, roaring its hatred.
He knows who you are. He knows what you are looking for.
And he will never let you go.
In a final act of survival, you launch the ship onto the coast, intentionally beaching it to escape the monster.
The Manticore, your home, your dream, remains there—hurt, but safe.
The months pass.
Your crew is adapting to this new life.
You find refuge in Zokmere, the sanctuary city, where all those who have been forgotten by the sea come.
One by one, your companions leave, following their own destiny.
Soon only Gregory remains.
Sitting on the edge of the quay, he sips his tea while watching the fishermen weigh anchor.
“It’s funny,” he said. “I think I always wanted to live here. » You join him, letting your legs dangle above the turquoise water.
“Sometimes we only know what we really want when the choice escapes us,” you answer.
“Maybe this life is worth as much as the one we would have had at home. » You look up at the sun.
“And I think I finally stopped crying for my father. » Gregory nods.
“Yes… but the Manticore? » A smile crosses your face.
“I don’t think I’ll ever be able to leave him. » Gregory stands up, places a hand on your shoulder.
“We wouldn’t have survived without you, Captain. THANKS. » He walks away towards his new office, and you stay there, facing the sea, listening to the surf caressing the grounded hull of your ship.

passages.title: The World of the Shipwrecked
passages.text:
There is no way to get home.
Without the totems, the gods will remain asleep, and the path to your world will remain sealed forever.
You look down at the deck of the Manticore, listening to the tired breathing of your crew.
“It’s time to accept reality,” you finally say.
“This world is not ours… but we can live in it.
And perhaps it is better to leave these people the peace they deserve. » You manage to return to the sea, but it doesn't take long for the Hectakron to resurface from the depths.
Its claws plow the hull, its howls make the sky tremble.
He stalks you, tirelessly, driven by an ancient hatred.
In a final act of survival, you throw the ship ashore, beaching the Manticore on shore to escape the creature.
Your vessel, your home, remains there, broken but standing — a silent monument to all you've been through.
The months pass.
Your crew is adjusting to their new life.
You find refuge in Zokmere, the sanctuary city, where all those who no longer have a port end up.
Little by little, your companions leave, each going their own way.
Only Gregory remains, faithful to the end.
Sitting on the edge of the quay, he sips his tea, watching the fishing boats sail away towards the horizon.
“It’s funny,” he said with a calm smile.
“I think I always wanted to live here, deep down. » You join him, feet suspended above the turquoise water.
“Sometimes you don’t know what you really want until the choice disappears,” you reply.
“And, in a way, I think this life is worth the one I would have had in New York. » You inhale deeply, the warmth of the sun filtering through the mist.
“And I think I finally stopped crying for my father. » Gregory nods gently.
“Yes… but the Manticore? » A slight smile stretches your lips.
“I don’t think I’ll ever be able to leave him. » Gregory stands up, places a hand on your shoulder.
“We would never have survived without you, Captain.
THANKS. » He slowly walks away towards his new medical office, leaving behind the sea and its changing reflections.
You stand there for a moment, listening to the salty wind caress the Manticore's hull, until the world seems, finally, at peace.
